findings.text: follow-on: _flux_blocks gained a required keyword-only `builder` parameter with no default, and an existing caller outside this node's write scope was not updated. scripts/accuracy_cost_ladder/measure.py:140 still calls fixture._flux_blocks(targets, polygons, geometry.atomic_mesh.centroids); this review reproduced `TypeError: _flux_blocks() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'builder'` at the reviewed head. This falsifies the resumed ruling's clause (1) claim that no existing caller changes behaviour — the host default preserves the host *behaviour*, but this caller no longer runs at all, and the delta lane (tests/test_coupling_build.py only) cannot see it. Fix is one line at the caller (builder=measure.BUILDER_HOST) or a default on the parameter; it belongs to a parser/scaffolding follow-on rather than to this node, whose declared write paths do not include scripts/accuracy_cost_ladder.

follow-on: the fragment cites logs/coupling_scale.sbatch beside logs/coupling_scale_driver.py as the way to reproduce the 5,000/10,000-cell timings, but at the reviewed head that pair no longer reproduces them. The driver calls measure.cached_machine(case, cells, wall_nodes=...) with no builder argument and neither the driver nor the sbatch sets NOVA_ANALYTIC_ORACLE_BUILDER, so after the resumed ruling made the host builder the default, resolve_builder() returns 'host' and the cited command now builds on the host path rather than the device path that produced 151.2 s and 271.3 s. The run that produced those figures (job 1283225, 2026-10-10 21:21 local) ran at ead33bdc3, before the gating commit, when the device path was the default; its published semantic keys ed99b1e5c21b1246 / 0e68c6590609a883 and its 75% GPU utilisation sample are consistent with device builds. The pointer should carry NOVA_ANALYTIC_ORACLE_BUILDER=device to remain reproducible.

follow-on: the module docstring states the packed kernel is the host reduction's device transcription and the blocks 'agree with the host analytic builder to round-off'. The node's own measurement contradicts that for the two moment channels: they differ by up to 1.05e-03 norm-relative at 550 cells and 6.58e-05 at 2,000 cells (h200_gap.1283232.log), and the fragment states plainly that the blocks do not meet 1e-10. The docstring should carry the same caveat the fragment and resolve_builder()'s docstring already carry, since it is the first thing a reader of the module sees. Minor: the manifest's artifacts line likewise reads 'as device-path carriers their groups are now 285afce3...' where the on-disk carriers were NOT re-keyed and still sit under the pre-builder groups; the fragment's re-key paragraph is the accurate statement.

follow-on: the resumed ruling's step (b) asks for the certificate map at the analytic limited AND diverted states; only the limited state was measured, because the analytic fixture family admits no diverted state (all three reference cases read diverted=False and the limiter wall has no X-point). The node reported this rather than passing it off, which is the right handling, but it means the ruling's (b) is satisfied for the limited half only. A later reader should not read the 9.70e-12 / 8.79e-12 map figures as covering a diverted configuration.

justifications.call_sites: Two call sites of the changed _flux_blocks exist at the reviewed head. measure.py's own _assemble_families passes builder=builder on both paths and is correct. scripts/accuracy_cost_ladder/measure.py:140 calls it with no builder and now raises TypeError — reproduced. No production solve path reaches either, which matches the node's scope.
justifications.durability: The guards are real and falsifiable, and I reproduced the falsification at the reviewed head rather than trusting the manifest: the identity check has genuine margin (35x on the uniform bound, 5.4x and 8.6x on the moment bounds at the guard's own case), and a 1e-9 relative perturbation to one entry is caught. Four tests pin the ruling's invariants (default is host; environment selects device; the two paths publish distinct keys differing only by builder; each path reaches its own builder). Below the top band for three reasons: the reviewed run's own negative_control.log was produced at an earlier revision (ead33bdc3, a two-test file) and so does not exercise the final six-test file — I had to re-derive it; adding builder and builder_revision to cache_identity changes every existing carrier's semantic group repo-wide, a durable consequence the node recorded but did not measure against the other modules whose tests consume those carriers; and the change left an out-of-scope caller raising TypeError, a failure no arm in this run could see.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced, not read. This review re-ran the head gate in the reviewed worktree at e5e794122: 6 passed in 21.54 s, EXIT=0 (review-head.log). It re-derived the negative control at head: an unperturbed run gives uniform/radial/vertical row gaps 2.875e-12 / 1. 867e-08 / 1.169e-08 against bounds 1e-10 / 1e-7 / 1e-7, and perturbing one block entry by 1e-9 relative lifts the uniform gap to 1.361e-10 — matching the reviewed run's negative_control.log to all printed digits — and the guard fires (review-negctl.log). The claims about the persisted carriers were checked against the stores themselves: analytic_oracle_hex_machine_5000.zarr sits under group ed99b1e5c21b1246 with builder_revision 2cf4dd873a1d455f and no builder field and wall_content.sha256 14f535f3934fef2c..., exactly as the fragment states (not re-keyed). The wall-content mismatch was independently recomputed: measure._resolved_wall(case, wall_nodes=121, wall=None) for moderate-rotation-conventional hashes to ad913c63c10e5e0af..., so the node's refusal to re-key rests on a real, reproduced difference. Read from the run's logs rather than re-run (heavy, H200): the gap job 1283232 and the 75%-GPU scale job 1283225.
justifications.fit: Follows the resumed ruling closely rather than widening the bound, which is exactly what was asked: the host builder stays the default, the device path is reachable only by argument or the NOVA_ANALYTIC_ORACLE_BUILDER environment variable, the criterion is restated against the quantity the carriers deliver (the map, not the block matrix), and the open construct is named and assigned to a node scoped to nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py. coupling_build.py assembles through nova.biot.tiledassembly.tile_evaluator with kernel='moments', so the device path is the same kernel the broad read already uses rather than a second assembly. The single fit deduction is the _flux_blocks signature change without a caller audit, which broke a script outside the scope and contradicts the ruling's own 'no existing caller changes behaviour' wording.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's own goal — batch the certificate machine coupling build on the device so 5,000 cells build within five minutes and 10,000 cells are metered and cached — is met: one H200 job (1283225) built 5,000 cells in 151.2 s wall (148.3 s build) and 10,000 cells in 271.3 s wall, both cold from an empty store root, both persisted under NOVA_ANALYTIC_ORACLE_CACHE with a 75% GPU utilisation sample, so the builds ran on the device. All four clauses of the resumed ruling (host default, builder in the cache identity, criterion (2) restated as the measured map pair, and the default/keys tests) landed at the reviewed head. Two deviations keep this below the top: the ruling's step (b) diverted half is not constructible in this fixture and was measured only at the limited state, and the ruling's clause (1) claim that no existing caller changes behaviour is falsified by the _flux_blocks signature break.
justifications.reuse: Reuses the existing kernels and helpers rather than adding a parallel mechanism: coupling_build.build_flux_blocks builds on nova.biot.polygon.pad_batch, nova.biot.polygonanalytic._horizontal_reflection and _section_centroid, and nova.biot.tiledassembly.TilePlan/tile_evaluator, and measure._flux_blocks swaps the reduction rather than duplicating it. The only new product code is one 122-line script module plus the small _assemble_families dispatch; the device branch shares the same pad/reflection/centroid construction the host path uses, so there is one packing and one geometry precompute.
justifications.scope_discipline: Four files changed across six commits, all inside the six declared write paths: scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/coupling_build.py (new, 122 lines), scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py (+100/-12), tests/test_coupling_build.py (new, 178 lines) and docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/cfs-coupling-build-scale.html (new, 308 lines); the diffstat over b86bfc728..e5e794122 reconciles at exactly these four. The three files the brief fences to concurrent nodes (nova/equilibrium/{forward,forward_operator,gs}.py) are untouched, as is nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py, which the node correctly left to a follow-on node. The one blemish is that changing a shared private helper's contract broke an out-of-scope caller without the node checking its callers, so the change's blast radius exceeds the boundary it declared — hence 17 rather than a clean 20.
